newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Week-long strike at Shell Gas Lanka, Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, ends after trade unions and company officials sign agreement on matters relating to transfers, incentives and allowances.
Parliament votes to extend emergency regulations that govern the country, by further month.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga's former press secretary arrested by police, with two others, for allegedly trying to fraudulently obtain $10 million from bank. Suspects released on bail.
Air force planes destroy communications centre of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in eastern Batticaloa jungles.
Five people killed by lightening and about 200 houses destroyed in a storm that hit northwestern province last Wednesday.
LTTE calls its leaders in the east to northern Mullaitivu to face army which is said to be preparing for major thurst into rebel-held northern Wanni region.
Shell Gas Lanka resumes gas distribution after strike that shut down operations for seven days and created countrywide shortages.
